name: Sui Mainnet
limits: Experimental: the engine is Mysten's sui-fork from sui-tools mainnet-v1.81.1, which Mysten marks highly experimental.
This is a private copy of Sui Mainnet: transactions run on the copy only and never appear on Sui Mainnet or its explorers.
Sui signatures do not bind to a chain, so a transaction signed for the copy is also valid on Sui Mainnet. Use test keys that hold no mainnet assets.
The copy serves Sui gRPC only, with grpc-web and no CORS layer. It serves no JSON-RPC and no GraphQL, so apps that read through GraphQL cannot run against it.
Transactions run one at a time, one per checkpoint, so runs are slow and cannot run in parallel.
The Clock (0x6) does not move unless chainsim advances it.
Dynamic-field listing is empty on the copy.

Funding is a transfer on the copy only, sent by impersonation with no signature from 0x935029ca5219502a47ac9b69f556ccf6e2198b5e7815cf50f68846f723739cbd, labeled Binance 1 at https://www.coincarp.com/currencies/sui/richlist/ and checked on Sui Mainnet on 2026-10-09 to hold 27.59 million SUI in address-owned coins. Nothing is sent on Sui Mainnet.
The funder's coins are seeded at up, which works only for fork points within about an hour of the upstream head, so fund fails on an older --block.
On Sui, fund only raises a balance: an address that already holds more than the amount asked is refused.
Snapshot and revert each stop and restart the engine to copy its data directory, so each takes a few seconds.
The engine runs as root inside its container, with all capabilities dropped, because the fork's data volume is root-owned and the sui-tools image has no other user.
There is no gas estimation: every transaction needs an explicit gas budget.
Objects the copy has not touched are read from the upstream GraphQL service on first access, so the first read of each object is slower.
Production wallets such as Slush submit through their own mainnet RPC, not the copy: a run needs a test wallet that can point at the copy.
